subject: Re: Model fit & quantization tradeoffs - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finwave.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Model fit & quantization tradeoffs - post-call recap

Alex - thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we're aligned: 

Highlights from today
- Primary goal: bring FinWave chat assistant latency down to <300ms median for short queries (<=60 tokens) while keeping quality within 2% of current baseline on your SLA prompt set.
- Secondary goal: reduce per-token cost by ~3-4x vs current hosted baseline for peak throughput periods.
- Key constraints: strict PII handling, data residency in us-east-1, and SLO-driven fallback behavior.

Initial model recommendations (based on your workload and prompt distribution)
- Mistral-7B (AWQ 4-bit) - Recommended low-latency path; good throughput and strong quality retention on instruction-style prompts.
- Llama-2-13B (FP16) - High-quality path for escalation/fallback; higher cost but minimal regression on edge cases.
- Falcon-40B (GPTQ 4-bit) - Cost-optimized path for batch/throughput mode; some risk of small quality delta on multi-turn financial context.

Quantization / throughput trade study notes
- AWQ: often preserves more of the fp16 accuracy at 4-bit on newer Mistral-style weights; promising for your latency targets.
- GPTQ: fast, widely supported, good TCO improvements; occasional regressions on long context finance prompts - needs eval.
- FP8 (where available on Dedicated infra): best for accuracy but requires newer runtime/hardware and slightly higher memory footprint vs 4-bit.

Requested artifacts (we agreed you'd share these)
- FinWave prompt set (v1) - helps us run the model-fit evals.
- A representative sample of 500-1,000 historical short queries for latency profiling.

Proposed immediate next steps
1) You share finwave-prompts-v1.txt (confirmed you will do this).
2) Redwood runs a 1,000-eval sweep across Mistral-7B (AWQ), Llama-2-13B (FP16), and Falcon-40B (GPTQ) using your prompts - we'll report ROU/accuracy deltas, latency P50/P95, and tokens/sec. (Owner: Marissa; target results by 2027-05-25).
3) Engineering deep-dive if we see >2% regression on any key prompt - Dylan to lead the technical review.
4) Draft MAP and schedule pilot for early June if results look good.

Attachments: finwave-prompts-v1.txt (please confirm final version), sample MAP template attached for your review.

Thanks - ccing Dylan and Rishi for technical and procurement context.


Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Model fit & quantization tradeoffs - post-call recap

Marissa - thanks for the thorough recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Quality tolerance: the business team will accept up to ~2% drop on intent classification/answer correctness for shorter queries, but NO regression on compliance/legal prompts (those must match current baseline).
2) Latency is priority for the consumer-facing assistant; for backend batch jobs we prefer cost-savings.

I've uploaded finwave-prompts-v1.txt to the drive link (same filename). Also attaching a small sample of 200 historical short queries for latency profiling. Can you confirm the eval will include: 
- per-prompt correctness (binary),
- hallucination flagging for free-text answers,
- latency P50/P95/P99, and
- token consumption/cost estimate per model variant.

Pilot timing: we're aiming to have a technical pilot started by the week of June 7 - can Redwood commit to delivering the initial eval results by 2027-05-25 as discussed?

Thanks - happy to sync quickly if needed.

Alex Johnson
Head of AI Product, FinWave
alex.johnson@finwave.com
Attachment: finwave-prompts-v1.txt (uploaded to Drive)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finwave.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model fit & quantization tradeoffs - technical notes

Alex / team - quick technical notes on the AWQ / GPTQ / FP8 tradeoffs and the eval plan we'll run: 

High-level:
- AWQ (4-bit): best candidate for Mistral-7B in our internal tests - often retains within ~1% of fp16 on instruction-following tasks while giving 2.5-3.5x throughput improvements depending on batching and KV cache effectiveness. Good low-latency characteristics when combined with continuous batching.
- GPTQ (4-bit): broadly supported, lower engineering setup time, good throughput gains. On some finance multi-turn prompts we've observed small regressions on numeric consistency and formatting (examples will be in the CSV).
- FP8: when available on Dedicated infra (specific GPUs/kernels), FP8 gets closest to fp16 accuracy but with less dramatic TCO improvements than 4-bit; requires a bit more tuning for memory allocation.

Planned eval metrics (we will deliver a CSV):
- per-prompt correctness (0/1), 3-judge majority for ambiguous answers
- hallucination flag (0/1) with short explanation where flagged
- response token count and estimated per-token cost (hosted vs dedicated)
- latency P50/P95 measured on our Dedicated staging in us-east-1 with realistic batching (batch sizes: 1, 4, 8)
- model size, quantization profile, and memory footprint per config

Recommended quick configs to test now:
- Mistral-7B (AWQ, 4-bit), batch sizes = 1/4, KV cache enabled for multi-turn
- Llama-2-13B (FP16), batch sizes = 1/2 (quality baseline)
- Falcon-40B (GPTQ, 4-bit), batch sizes = 4/8 for throughput mode

We'll run the 1k-eval sweep Marissa requested and produce: finwave-eval-results.csv and a short trade-study PDF with per-case callouts. If we see >2% regression on any compliance/legal prompt we will stop and escalate to manual tuning (and exclude that quantized config from pilot).

ETA: results and artifacts by 2027-05-25 EOD Pacific. Can you confirm we have permission to run these models on your provided prompt set and to store the eval artifacts in our secure project folder?


Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: quant-trade-study.pdf (summary + charts)

Alex - great, thanks for confirming. We have permission to run the evals on the prompt set you uploaded and will store the artifacts in the secure Drive folder linked below. Summary / next steps and owners: 

1) Redwood to run 1k eval sweep (Mistral-7B AWQ, Llama-2-13B FP16, Falcon-40B GPTQ) - deliverables: finwave-eval-results.csv, quant-trade-study.pdf (Owner: Dylan; Due: 2027-05-25 EOD PT).
2) Safety/compliance check: Rishi to review all compliance/legal prompts within 24 hours of results and flag any regressions (Owner: Rishi; Due: 2027-05-26).
3) MAP + Pilot scheduling: Marissa to send pilot plan and proposed SOW for June start (Owner: Marissa; Due: 2027-05-27).

If results look good we'll propose the following operational plan for the pilot: 
- Primary path: Mistral-7B (AWQ) on Dedicated pool for consumer assistant with continuous batching + prefix caching.
- Fallback path: Llama-2-13B (FP16) for compliance-sensitive calls.
- Cost path: Falcon-40B (GPTQ) for backend batch inference.

We'll flag any config that fails the 2% quality gate for compliance prompts and pause that config from pilot inclusion.

Meeting: I'll propose a 30-min sync for Fri 2027-06-04 to review results and agree pilot SOW. Please let me know if that works on your end.
